overview: This Senate resolution condemns the Chinese government's actions in Hong Kong, the former British territory that returned to Chinese rule in 1997 with promises that it would keep its own freedoms and legal system. It condemns the 2020 national security law imposed by Beijing and a 2024 Hong Kong security law, saying they have been used to bring politically motivated charges against people for exercising basic rights. It calls on Hong Kong to drop such charges and free those held, including newspaper publisher Jimmy Lai, says Hong Kong has lost credibility as an international business center, and urges the U.S. to treat Hong Kong and mainland China the same in international voting and to use existing tools such as the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act. The resolution expresses the Senate's view and does not impose any new sanctions itself. As of April 28, 2025, the Senate Foreign Relations Committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say the resolution puts the Senate on record in defense of Hong Kongers' basic freedoms and urges the U.S. to hold Beijing accountable for breaking its promises.
against: Critics say the resolution is largely symbolic, and its claims about Hong Kong's business climate and calls to treat it the same as mainland China could hurt Americans and companies still working there.
